directive:
Target `thm:uniform-boolean-operator` directly; do not try to prove `oeq:dense-four-root-switching` term by term. Work throughout under the uniform simple \(d\)-regular law with \(n^{2/5}\le d=o(\sqrt n)\). Put
\[
C_{ij}=(A^2)_{ij},\qquad
B_{ij}=A_{ij}+(1-A_{ij})\mathbf 1\{C_{ij}\ge1\}\quad(i\ne j).
\]
Let \(\eta=d^2/n=o(1)\), choose
\[
K=\left\lceil\frac{20\log n}{\log(1/\eta)}\right\rceil
\]
once \(\eta<1/2\), and define
\[
S_K(c)=\sum_{r=1}^K(-1)^{r+1}\binom cr,\qquad
Q_{ij}=A_{ij}+(1-A_{ij})S_K(C_{ij}),\quad Q_{ii}=1.
\]
This truncation has the exact remainder
\[
|B_{ij}-Q_{ij}|=(1-A_{ij})\binom{C_{ij}-1}{K}\mathbf1\{C_{ij}>K\}.
\tag{D1}
\]
First prove, by the marked residual-completion switching on the simple regular law, uniformly for \(m\le2K+2\),
\[
\mathbb E(C_{12})_m\le (1+o(1))^m\eta^m,
\tag{D2}
\]
with an error whose logarithm is \(o(K\log(1/\eta))\). Use the product identity for two binomial coefficients and (D1) to deduce
\[
n^2\mathbb E(B_{12}-Q_{12})^2=o(d^{7/2}).
\tag{D3}
\]
Consequently \(\|(B-Q)P\|_{\rm op}\le\|B-Q\|_F=o_P(d^{7/4})\). Do not transfer (D2) from the configuration model by conditioning on simplicity; prove it with completion switchings.

For \(Q\), do not bound the individual inclusion--exclusion monomials. Rewrite the entire polynomial \(S_K(C_{ij})-\mathbb ES_K(C_{12})\) in the factorial/Poisson--Charlier basis with parameter \(\eta\), and retain each Charlier block intact in the trace expansion. The subtraction of the exact marginal mean and the right projection \(P\) delete the rank-one block; Charlier degeneracy cancels every diagram containing a witness-tree component attached to only one rooted block. Thus every surviving trace diagram is a no-floating Xu shape, or contains an explicit collision joining two formerly separate witness blocks.

Apply Xu Section 2.2, Theorems 14--15 through the Section 2.3 block-value trace-walk formulation to this grouped polynomial, with trace order
\[
\ell=\left\lceil 10\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right\rceil.
\]
Verify explicitly that the total shape size is polylogarithmic and \(<d^{1/10}\), using \(d\ge n^{2/5}\), and prove the grouped estimate
\[
\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}\!\left[(P(Q-\mathbb EQ)P)^{2\ell}\right]
\le n\bigl(d^{3/2+o(1)}\bigr)^{2\ell}.
\tag{D4}
\]
Here the \(o(1)\) must be uniform over all \(d=o(\sqrt n)\). Account separately for direct root edges and repeated witnesses; each repeated-witness identification removes a free vertex and supplies at least the compensating \(1/n\) factor. Do not sum absolute values before the Charlier/floating-tree cancellation. Since \(d\ge n^{2/5}\), \(d^{3/2+o(1)}=o(d^{7/4})\), and (D4) gives
\[
\|QP\|_{\rm op}=o_P(d^{7/4}).
\tag{D5}
\]
Combining (D3) and (D5) proves the dense branch of `thm:uniform-boolean-operator`; splice it with the proved sparse branch.

As an internal check, expand the fourth trace of the grouped Charlier expression. Its four-distinct-root contribution must reproduce
\[
\mu_{\rm cyc}=s-4pt+p^2(4a+2b)-3p^4.
\]
The separate-witness \(p^4\)-scale diagrams must disappear inside the grouped floating-tree cancellation, while connected collision diagrams are \(O(d^4/n^3)\). If Xu's block-value theorem cannot be instantiated with growing \(K\) with constants small enough for (D4), report that failure explicitly: invoking the theorem shape-by-shape or merely asserting Charlier cancellation is not a faithful closure.

Target `thm:uniform-boolean-operator` via a collision-discrepancy argument genuinely different from the failed Xu/Charlier route. Put
\[
W=A^2+A-(d-1)I,\qquad E=W-B.
\]
Then \(E_{ii}=0\), while for \(i\ne j\), \(E_{ij}=W_{ij}-\mathbf1\{W_{ij}>0\}\ge0\). By vertex exchangeability, \(\mathbb EE=\alpha(J-I)\) for a scalar \(\alpha\), and hence, with \(H=E-\mathbb EE\),
\[
EP=HP-\alpha P. \tag{C1}
\]
This identity handles the entire right-projected operator; do not replace \(HP\) by \(PHP\).

Prove the following collision-discrepancy lemma directly by simple-completion switchings. For every deterministic \(S,T\subset[n]\), let \(Z_{S,T}=\sum_{i\in S,j\in T}E_{ij}\) and \(\mu_{S,T}=\mathbb EZ_{S,T}\). Uniformly for \(n^{2/5}\le d=o(\sqrt n)\), establish
\[
\Pr\{|Z_{S,T}-\mu_{S,T}|\ge t\}\le2\exp\left[-c\min\left\{\frac{t^2}{d\mu_{S,T}+d^2(|S|+|T|)+1},\frac td\right\}\right]. \tag{C2}
\]
It is sufficient with additional universal polylogarithmic factors. Reveal a uniformly selected valid oriented two-switch and pair completions with \(Z_{S,T}\) increased or decreased. One switch changes only the two switched endpoint rows and their old/new neighbor columns, so \(|\Delta Z_{S,T}|\le Cd\). Charge an increasing switch either to an existing collision counted by \(Z_{S,T}\), or to one of the \(O(d^2(|S|+|T|))\) boundary incidences created at a switched endpoint. After normalizing by the \(\asymp(nd)^2\) valid oriented switches, prove
\[
\mathbb E[(\Delta Z_{S,T})^2\mid G]\le\frac{C}{nd}\bigl(dZ_{S,T}+d^2(|S|+|T|)\bigr). \tag{C4}
\]
Apply the standard exchangeable-pair/Freedman argument, including the reverse-switch comparison, to obtain (C2). Do not cite bounded differences alone.

Use the already proved completion-switching factorial bound to obtain
\[
\alpha\le C\frac{d^4}{n^2},\qquad \max_i\mathbb E\sum_jE_{ij}\le C\rho,\qquad \rho=d^4/n. \tag{C5}
\]
Then use (C2), dyadic cardinality classes, and a union bound over \(S,T\) for the simultaneous Feige--Ofek discrepancy alternative
\[
\left|\sum_{i\in S,j\in T}H_{ij}\right|\le C\left[\sqrt{d\rho|S||T|}\log^C n+d(|S|+|T|)\log^C n\right]. \tag{C6}
\]
The standard light/heavy-coordinate decomposition should yield
\[
\|H\|_{\rm op}\le C(\sqrt{d\rho}+d)\log^C n=C\left(\frac{d^{5/2}}{\sqrt n}+d\right)\log^C n=o(d^{7/4}), \tag{C7}
\]
using \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), \(d\ge n^{2/5}\), and that fixed polylogarithms are \(o(d^{1/4})\). Also \(\alpha=o(d^{7/4})\). Cook--Goldstein--Johnson gives
\[
\|WP\|_{\rm op}\le\|AP\|_{\rm op}^2+\|AP\|_{\rm op}+d-1=O(d). \tag{C9}
\]
Combine \(BP=WP-EP\) with (C1), (C7), and (C9) to prove the dense branch, then splice with the proved sparse branch.

Treat (C2), specifically the variance-sensitive switching count (C4), as the sole new obligation. If the forward/reverse switch count cannot prove (C4), report that failure explicitly: ordinary adjacency spectrum, generic Efron--Stein, fixed-shape graph-matrix bounds, and the completed truncation estimate do not imply it. Do not return to the failed Xu/Charlier construction.
